topics.label: Introduction to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation within the Biology of Disease course.

topics.label: Principles of innate pathogen and danger recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through conserved PAMPs, DAMPs, and germline-encoded pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major families of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling cascades, and the assembly of the inflammasome to process inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Inflammatory cell recruitment, trafficking, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular actions and trafficking events that drive the inflammatory response and the severe pathologies that arise when systemic activation occurs.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue repair, and result in chronic inflammation or granuloma formation when clearance fails.

topics.label: Conclusion to the lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on complement.
